devdoc.author: Angle Core Team
devdoc.details: This file contains the front end, that is all external functions associated to the given stablecoin

accumulateInterest(uint256).details: This function is called by a `PoolManager` contract having some yield farming strategies associatedTo prevent flash loans, the `sanRate` is not directly updated, it is updated at the blocks that follow

addGovernor(address).details: This function propagates changes from `Core` to other contractsPropagating changes like that allows to maintain the protocol's integrity

burn(uint256,address,address,address,uin.details: The `msg.sender` should have approval to burn from the `burner` or the `msg.sender` should be the `burner`If there are not enough reserves this transaction will revert and the user will have to come back to the protocol with a correct amount. Checking for the reserves currently available in the `PoolManager` is something that should be handled by the front interacting with this contractIn case there are not enough reserves, strategies should be harvested or their debt ratios should be adjusted by governance to make sure that users, HAs or SLPs withdrawing always have free collateral they can useFrom a user perspective, this function is equivalent to a swap from stablecoins to collateral

params.burner: Address from which the agTokens will be burnt
params.dest: Address where collateral is going to be
params.minCollatAmount: Minimum amount of collateral that the user is willing to get for this transaction
params.poolManager: Collateral type requested by the user burning

convertToSLP(uint256,address).details: Can only be called by a `PerpetualManager` contractThis is typically useful when a HA wishes to cash out but there is not enough collateral in reserves

deploy(address[],address,address).details: This function is called by the `Core` when a stablecoin is deployed to maintain consistency across the governor and guardian rolesWhen this function is called by the `Core`, it has already been checked that the `stableMaster` corresponding to the `agToken` was this `stableMaster`

params._agToken: Reference to the `AgToken`, that is the ERC20 token handled by the `StableMaster`
params.governorList: List of the governor addresses of the protocol

deployCollateral(address,address,address.details: All the references in parameters should correspond to contracts that have already been deployed and initialized with appropriate referencesAfter calling this function, governance should initialize all parameters corresponding to this new collateral

params.oracle: Reference to the oracle that will give the price of the collateral with respect to the stablecoin
params.perpetualManager: Contract managing HA perpetuals for this stablecoin
params.poolManager: Contract managing and storing this collateral for this stablecoin
params.sanToken: Reference to the sanTokens associated to the collateral

params.poolManager: Address of the `PoolManager` of the required collateral
params.user: Address of the SLP to send sanTokens to

getCollateralRatio().details: The ratio returned is scaled by `BASE_PARAMS` since the value is used to in the `FeeManager` contrat to be compared with the values in `xArrays` expressed in `BASE_PARAMS`The collateral ratio computed here does not take into account the total supply of the stablecoin since stablecoins can be minted in other places than in this moduleThis means that parameters depending on collateral ratio like slippage will strictly depend on what's going on in this module: like if this module is under-collateralized but other modules are functioning well, slippage will still apply to SLPs here

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

getStocksUsers().details: This function will not return something relevant if it is not called by a `PerpetualManager`

returns._stocksUsers: All stablecoins currently assigned to the pool of the caller

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.

params.core_: Address of the `Core` contract handling all the different `StableMaster` contracts

mint(uint256,address,address,uint256).details: This function works as a swap from a user perspective from collateral to stablecoinsIt is impossible to mint tokens and to have them sent to the zero address: there would be an issue with the `_mint` function called by the `AgToken` contractThe parameter `minStableAmount` serves as a slippage protection for usersFrom a user perspective, this function is equivalent to a swap between collateral and stablecoins

params.minStableAmount: Minimum amount of stablecoins the user wants to get with this transaction
params.poolManager: Address of the `PoolManager` of the required collateral
params.user: Address of the contract or the person to give the minted tokens to

pause(bytes32,address).details: If agent is `STABLE`, it is going to be impossible for users to mint stablecoins using collateral or to burn their stablecoinsIf agent is `SLP`, it is going to be impossible for SLPs to deposit collateral and receive sanTokens in exchange, or to withdraw collateral from their sanTokens

params.agent: Bytes representing the agent (`SLP` or `STABLE`) and the collateral type that is going to be paused. To get the `bytes32` from a string, we use in Solidity a `keccak256` function
params.poolManager: Reference to the contract managing this collateral for this stablecoin in the protocol and for which `agent` needs to be paused

rebalanceStocksUsers(uint256,address,add.details: This function can be called in case where the reserves of the protocol for each collateral do not exactly match what is stored in the `stocksUsers` because of increases or decreases in collateral prices at times in which the protocol was not fully hedged by HAsWith this function, governance can allow/prevent more HAs coming in a pool while preventing/allowing HAs from other pools because the accounting variable of `stocksUsers` does not really match

params.amount: Amount of `stocksUsers` to transfer from a pool to another
params.poolManagerDown: Reference to `PoolManager` for which `stocksUsers` needs to decrease
params.poolManagerUp: Reference to `PoolManager` for which `stocksUsers` needs to increase

removeGovernor(address).details: This function propagates changes from `Core` to other contractsPropagating changes like that allows to maintain the protocol's integrityIt has already been checked in the `Core` that this address could be removed and that it would not put the protocol in a situation with no governor at all

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `account`.

revokeCollateral(address,address).details: Since this function has the ability to transfer the contract's funds to another contract, it should only be accessible to the governorBefore calling this function, governance should make sure that all the collateral lent to strategies has been withdrawn

params.poolManager: Reference to the contract managing this collateral for this stablecoin in the protocol
params.settlementContract: Settlement contract that will be used to close everyone's positions and to let users, SLPs and HAs redeem if not all a portion of their claim

revokeGuardian(address).details: This function propagates changes from `Core` to other contracts

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.

params._maxInterestsDistributed: Maximum amount of interests distributed to SLPs in a block
params.poolManager: Reference to the `PoolManager` contract associated to the collateral

setCore(address).details: This function can only be called by the `Core` contract

params._bonusMalusBurn: New corrector of user burn fees, depending on collateral ratio
params._bonusMalusMint: New corrector of user mint fees for this collateral. These fees will correct the mint fees from users that just depend on the hedge curve by HAs by introducing other dependencies. In normal times they will be equal to `BASE_PARAMS` meaning fees will just depend on the hedge ratio
params._slippage: New global slippage (the SLP fees from withdrawing) factor
params._slippageFee: New global slippage fee (the non distributed accumulated fees) factor

params.poolManager: Reference to the contract managing this collateral for this stablecoin in the protocol and associated to the `FeeManager` to update

setGuardian(address,address).details: This function propagates changes from `Core` to other contractsThe zero check for the guardian address has already been performed by the `Core` contract

setIncentivesForSLPs(uint64,uint64,addre.details: The higher these proportions the bigger the APY for SLPsThese proportions should be inferior to `BASE_PARAMS`

params._feesForSLPs: New proportion of mint/burn fees going to SLPs
params._interestsForSLPs: New proportion of interests from lending going to SLPs

params._oracle: New oracle contract for the pair collateral/stablecoin
params.poolManager: Reference to the `PoolManager` contract associated to the collateral

setTargetHAHedge(uint64).details: Can only be called by the `PerpetualManager`

params._targetHAHedge: New value of the hedge ratio that the protocol wants to arrive to

setUserFees(address,uint64[],uint64[],ui.details: The evolution of the fees between two thresholds is linearThe length of the two arrays should be the sameThe values of `_xFee` should be in ascending orderFor mint fees, values in the y-array below should normally be decreasing: the higher the `x` the cheaper it should be for stable seekers to come in as a high `x` corresponds to a high demand for volatility and hence to a situation where all the collateral can be hedgedFor burn fees, values in the array below should normally be decreasing: the lower the `x` the cheaper it should be for stable seekers to go out, as a low `x` corresponds to low demand for volatility and hence to a situation where the protocol has a hard time covering its collateral

params._mint: Whether mint fees or burn fees should be updated
params._yFee: Values of the fees at thresholds
params.poolManager: Reference to the `PoolManager` handling the collateral

signalLoss(uint256).details: This function is called by a `PoolManager` contract having some yield farming strategies associatedFees are not accumulated for this function before being distributed: everything is directly used to update the `sanRate`

params.loss: Loss made by the yield farming strategy

unpause(bytes32,address).details: Before calling this function, the agent should have been paused for this collateral

params.agent: Agent (`SLP` or `STABLE`) to unpause the action of

updateStocksUsers(uint256,address).details: This function can be called by the `agToken` contract after a burn of agTokens for which no collateral has been redeemed

params.poolManager: Reference to `PoolManager` for which `stocksUsers` needs to be updated

withdraw(uint256,address,address,address.details: The `msg.sender` should have approval to burn from the `burner` or the `msg.sender` should be the `burner`This transaction will fail if the `PoolManager` does not have enough reserves, the front will however be here to notify them that they cannot withdrawIn case there are not enough reserves, strategies should be harvested or their debt ratios should be adjusted by governance to make sure that users, HAs or SLPs withdrawing always have free collateral they can use

params.amount: Amount of sanTokens burnt by the SLP
params.burner: Address that will burn its sanTokens
params.dest: Address that will receive the collateral
params.poolManager: Address of the `PoolManager` of the required collateral

devdoc.title: StableMasterFront

BASE_PARAMS().notice: Base that is used to define parameters that need to have a floating value (for instance parameters that are defined as ratios)

BASE_TOKENS().notice: Base that is used to compute ratios and floating numbers

CORE_ROLE().notice: Role for `Core` only, used to propagate guardian and governors

accumulateInterest(uint256).notice: Takes into account the gains made while lending and distributes it to SLPs by updating the `sanRate`

agToken().notice: Reference to the `AgToken` used in this `StableMaster` This reference cannot be changed

burn(uint256,address,address,address,uin.notice: Lets a user burn agTokens (stablecoins) and receive the collateral specified by the `poolManager` in exchange

collateralMap(address).notice: Maps a `PoolManager` contract handling a collateral for this stablecoin to the properties of the struct above

convertToSLP(uint256,address).notice: Transforms a HA position into a SLP Position

deploy(address[],address,address).notice: Creates the access control logic for the governor and guardian addresses

deployCollateral(address,address,address.notice: Deploys a new collateral by creating the correct references in the corresponding contracts

deposit(uint256,address,address).notice: Lets a SLP enter the protocol by sending collateral to the system in exchange of sanTokens

getCollateralRatio().notice: Returns the collateral ratio for this stablecoin

getStocksUsers().notice: Transmits to the `PerpetualManager` the max amount of collateral (in stablecoin value) HAs can hedge

mint(uint256,address,address,uint256).notice: Lets a user send collateral to the system to mint stablecoins

pause(bytes32,address).notice: Pauses an agent's actions within this contract for a given collateral type for this stablecoin

rebalanceStocksUsers(uint256,address,add.notice: Updates the `stocksUsers` for a given pair of collateral

removeGovernor(address).notice: Removes a governor address which loses its role

revokeCollateral(address,address).notice: Removes a collateral from the list of accepted collateral types and pauses all actions associated to this collateral

setCapOnStableAndMaxInterests(uint256,ui.notice: Changes the parameters to cap the number of stablecoins you can issue using one collateral type and the maximum interests you can distribute to SLPs in a sanRate update in a block

setFeeKeeper(uint64,uint64,uint64,uint64.notice: Updates all the fees not depending on personal agents inputs via a keeper calling the corresponding function in the `FeeManager` contract

setFeeManager(address,address,address).notice: Sets a new `FeeManager` contract and removes the old one which becomes useless

setIncentivesForSLPs(uint64,uint64,addre.notice: Sets the proportion of fees from burn/mint of users and the proportion of lending interests going to SLPs

setOracle(address,address).notice: Propagates the change of oracle for one collateral to all the contracts which need to have the correct oracle reference

setTargetHAHedge(uint64).notice: Sets the proportion of `stocksUsers` available for perpetuals

setUserFees(address,uint64[],uint64[],ui.notice: Sets the x array (ie ratios between amount hedged by HAs and amount to hedge) and the y array (ie values of fees at thresholds) used to compute mint and burn fees for users

signalLoss(uint256).notice: Takes into account a loss made by a yield farming strategy

unpause(bytes32,address).notice: Unpauses an agent's action for a given collateral type for this stablecoin

updateStocksUsers(uint256,address).notice: Allows the `agToken` contract to update the `stocksUsers` for a given collateral after a burn with no redeem

withdraw(uint256,address,address,address.notice: Lets a SLP burn of sanTokens and receive the corresponding collateral back in exchange at the current exchange rate between sanTokens and collateral

userdoc.notice: `StableMaster` is the contract handling all the collateral types accepted for a given stablecoin It does all the accounting and is the point of entry in the protocol for stable holders and seekers as well as SLPs
